subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should systemd-managed Gateway turns support provider API keys from `openclaw.json` `env`, or should durable provider keys for managed services be required to live in per-agent auth profiles or SecretRefs?
rationale: Current source already applies config env during snapshot reads, but the reported shipped failure and managed-env marker/status behavior show the user-facing credential contract is still ambiguous and compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Support config env in Gateway
options.body: Make `openclaw.json` `env` a tested supported source for managed Gateway turns, with startup health checks and status wording matching that runtime path.

options.title: Require stored auth profiles
options.body: Change docs and diagnostics to steer managed-service provider keys into per-agent auth profiles or SecretRefs and stop presenting config env as effective runtime auth for that mode.

options.title: Split by explicit mode
options.body: Keep current compatibility behavior but add a clear opt-in strict or service-secret mode with docs and upgrade warnings.

recommendation.title: Support config env in Gateway
recommendation.body: Make `openclaw.json` `env` a tested supported source for managed Gateway turns, with startup health checks and status wording matching that runtime path.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is mostly in the daemon/service-env and systemd runtime contract, where recent history points most strongly to vincentkoc.
